confirmedFindings.summary: The drift script treats any non-zero `prisma migrate status` as a fatal error, but Prisma exits 1 permanently on the diverged-history state this repo deliberately created when it baselined production in #349 — so the gate can never reach the diff on prod.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Verified in the Prisma 7.10 CLI bundle (`node_modules/prisma/build/cli.js`): `migrate status` calls `process.exit(1)` unconditionally when `diagnoseMigrationHistory` returns `historiesDiverge` — the branch that prints "The migrations from the database are not found locally in prisma/migrations". `historiesDiverge` fires whenever `_prisma_migrations` holds rows for migrations absent from `prisma/migrations`, independently of whether anything is pending.

Commit 63376fe7 ("fix(db): baseline migrations against the real production schema (#349)") instructs existing environments to run `prisma migrate resolve --applied 0_init`. `migrate resolve --applied` only INSERTS the `0_init` row; it does not delete the pre-baseline rows. Every environment baselined that way therefore stays in `historiesDiverge` forever.

I reproduced exactly this against the running routeflow compose Postgres (read-only): `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev node apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs` printed `Your local migration history and the migrations table from your database are different: ... The migrations from the database are not found locally in prisma/migrations: 20260310041311_init, 20260310043525_add_routestop_customer_fk, ...` then `schema-drift: migrate status failed`, exit 1. The `migrate diff` step never ran.

Failure scenario: an operator follows CLAUDE.md's deploy flow and runs `railway run --service postgres node apps/api/scripts/prod-migrate.mjs`. `migrate deploy` succeeds, then the new post-deploy block (prod-migrate.mjs:50-60) spawns schema-drift.mjs, which exits 1 on the diverged history, so prod-migrate prints `post-deploy drift check FAILED` and exits non-zero after a SUCCESSFUL production migration. The same thing makes `npm run local:validate` (CLAUDE.md's documented pre-PR gate, now chained to `local:drift`) go red on any compose volume carrying pre-baseline rows — reproduced above. CI will not catch it: the db-migrations job runs against a fresh Postgres with a clean history, so the drift step there is green.

Caveat I cannot close from this machine: I did not read production's `_prisma_migrations` table, so the prod claim rests on #349's own resolve-only instruction plus the identical state observed on a routeflow database. Exit-code conflation is real regardless — a pending/diverged history is reported as exit 1 with the message "migrate status failed", not as drift (exit 2), and with no remediation hint.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Do not let a non-zero `migrate status` be fatal on its own. Either (a) run `migrate status` for information only (capture output, do not gate on its exit code) and let `migrate diff --exit-code` be the sole verdict, or (b) parse the status output and fail only on `failedMigrationNames` / `databaseIsBehind`, tolerating `historiesDiverge` with an explicit warning that names the orphan migrations. Whichever is chosen, the message must distinguish "pending migrations", "diverged history" and "could not reach the database", and prod-migrate must not report a successful deploy as FAILED.

confirmedFindings.summary: Switching to the shared helper deleted the script's hard guard: a partially-missing Railway proxy env now silently falls back to whatever `DATABASE_URL` is in the environment and prints `Target host: undefined:undefined`, so a mis-invoked prod migration runs against an unintended database with no visible target.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Before this change (old lines 22-36) the script computed `missing = need.filter(...)` and, if ANY of POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / POSTGRES_DB / RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN / RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT was absent, printed `Missing env: <list>` and exited 1 unconditionally. Now `resolveDatabaseUrl` (apps/api/scripts/lib/railway-db-url.mjs:24) returns `env.DATABASE_URL` whenever it is set, and the script proceeds.

Reproduced on this tree, with every proxy var unset and only DATABASE_URL present:

  env -u POSTGRES_USER -u POSTGRES_PASSWORD -u POSTGRES_DB -u RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN -u RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT \
    DATABASE_URL="postgresql://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/nope" node scripts/prod-migrate.mjs

Output:
  Target host: undefined:undefined
  === prisma migrate status ===
  ... Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "nope" ... at "127.0.0.1:1"
  === prisma migrate deploy ===
  ... at "127.0.0.1:1"

So `prisma migrate deploy` was actually issued against the fallback URL (it only stopped because the port was closed). Concrete failure scenario: an operator types `railway run --service api node apps/api/scripts/prod-migrate.mjs` (wrong service). The `api` service injects DATABASE_URL but none of the postgres proxy vars. Old code: clean abort naming the missing vars. New code: proceeds against the injected URL, and line 36 still reads `e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN`/`e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT`, so the one line that tells the operator what is being migrated prints `Target host: undefined:undefined`. The same applies to any shell that happens to export DATABASE_URL.

This also directly violates the build plan's p3 directive (build-plan.md:143-145): "keep the `need`/error semantics identical". The implementing engineer reported the deviation but did not fix it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Restore the pre-check in prod-migrate.mjs: before calling the helper, compute the missing proxy vars from `RAILWAY_PROXY_VARS` and exit 1 with the original `Missing env: <list>` + "Run this via: railway run --service postgres ..." message — this script must not accept a DATABASE_URL fallback. Separately, replace line 36's `Target host: ${e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN}:${e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT}` with `redactUrl(url)` so the printed target always matches the URL actually used.

confirmedFindings.summary: `describeDb`'s skip path does not actually skip: Jest evaluates a `describe.skip` body, so `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()` still runs and the DB lane fails to run instead of being skipped when DATABASE_URL is unset.
confirmedFindings.detail:
`describeDb` (apps/api/src/common/testing/db-spec.ts:16) routes to `describe.skip` when RUN_DB_SPECS is unset. I probed Jest's actual behaviour by adding a temporary spec containing `describe.skip("outer", () => { console.log("SKIP_BODY_EVALUATED"); it(...) })` and running it: the console line printed while the test reported "1 skipped". jest-circus evaluates a skipped describe's callback to collect its children; only the tests are marked skipped.

Because db-lane.db.spec.ts calls `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()` at line 7 — inside the describeDb callback — that call executes regardless of the skip. Reproduced with the lane's own config:

  cd apps/api && env -u DATABASE_URL -u RUN_DB_SPECS npx jest --config jest.db.config.js
  FAIL src/common/testing/db-lane.db.spec.ts
    ● Test suite failed to run
      DB-backed specs need DATABASE_URL — run `npm run local:test:db`
  Test Suites: 1 failed, 1 total   Tests: 0 total

`test:db` is a published script in apps/api/package.json with no env of its own, so a developer who runs `npm run test:db -w apps/api` (the obvious way to try the new lane) gets a red "Test suite failed to run" instead of the intended skip. Secondary effect on the other branch: when DATABASE_URL happens to be set but RUN_DB_SPECS is not, the `Pool` and `PrismaClient` at lines 8-10 are still constructed while `afterAll` never runs, so nothing disconnects them.

Verified working paths, for contrast: `RUN_DB_SPECS=local DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev npx jest --config jest.db.config.js` passes (1 test), and the CI step sets both, so CI is unaffected — this only bites the local/no-env invocation the skip gate exists to serve.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move the env-dependent work off the collection path: either have `describeDb` not invoke `fn` at all when disabled (e.g. `if (!process.env.RUN_DB_SPECS) return describe.skip(name, () => { it.skip("skipped: RUN_DB_SPECS unset", () => {}); })`), or keep the body inert by resolving the connection string inside `beforeAll` and constructing the Pool/PrismaClient there, with `afterAll` guarded for the never-constructed case.

confirmedFindings.summary: `scrubSecrets` fails open: when the URL password is not a valid percent-encoding, `decodeURIComponent` throws and the catch returns the ORIGINAL unscrubbed text, so the password would pass straight through to stdout/stderr.
confirmedFindings.detail:
The three `.split(...).join("***")` calls are chained inside one `try`, and the last one evaluates `decodeURIComponent(p)`. `decodeURIComponent` throws `URIError: URI malformed` for a lone `%` (verified: `decodeURIComponent('a%b')` → URIError). Because the throw happens before the `return`, the partially scrubbed result is discarded and the `catch` returns `text` verbatim.

Reproduced against the shipped helper:

  scrubSecrets('leak: pa%ss here', 'postgresql://u:pa%ss@h:5432/d')
  → "leak: pa%ss here"        (unchanged — the password was NOT redacted)

versus the well-formed case, which works: `scrubSecrets('leak: pa%ss here', 'postgresql://u:pa%25ss@h:5432/d')` → `"leak: *** here"`.

Failure scenario: `DATABASE_URL` is set with a raw `%` in the password (a hand-written URL, or a generated password containing `%` that was not percent-encoded). schema-drift.mjs:76-77 then writes prisma's stdout/stderr through this function believing it is redacted, and any echo of the credential reaches the console/CI log in the clear. The T3 spec only exercises `p w`/`p%20w`, which decodes cleanly, so the existing tests cannot catch this. The same throw also degrades `redactUrl` (line 33 decodes the username) to `"<unparseable url>"`.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Scrub each variant independently and never let a decode failure discard the work already done — e.g. build a candidate list `[p, encodeURIComponent(p), safeDecode(p)]` where `safeDecode` returns `null` on URIError, filter out empties/nulls, and apply the splits outside the try. The function must return at-least-partially-scrubbed text on every path, never the raw input.

confirmedFindings.summary: The `"::1"` entry in LOCAL_HOSTS is unreachable — WHATWG `URL.hostname` returns IPv6 hosts wrapped in brackets, so a loopback IPv6 DATABASE_URL is rejected as non-local.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Verified: `new URL('postgresql://u:p@[::1]:5432/x').hostname` returns the string `"[::1]"`, not `"::1"`. `LOCAL_HOSTS.has("[::1]")` is false, so requireLocalDatabaseUrl throws `Refusing to run DB-backed specs against non-local host [::1]`.

Failure scenario: a developer whose local Postgres resolves over IPv6 sets `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@[::1]:5432/routeflow_dev` and runs `npm run local:test:db`; the lane refuses to run against what is in fact loopback, with a message implying they are pointed at a remote host. The guard fails closed (safe direction), but the entry is dead as written and the diagnosis is misleading.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `"[::1]"` to LOCAL_HOSTS (keeping `"::1"` is harmless), or normalize with `host.replace(/^\[|\]$/g, "")` before the lookup.

confirmedFindings.summary: Spreading `package.json.jest` carries the campaign reporter (artifact "api") into the DB lane, so running `test:db` overwrites `.campaign/runs/api.json` with only the one db-lane result.
confirmedFindings.detail:
`const base = require("./package.json").jest;` pulls in `reporters: ["default", ["<rootDir>/../../../scripts/jest-campaign-reporter.cjs", { artifact: "api" }]]`, and the config overrides only testRegex/testPathIgnorePatterns/testTimeout. `scripts/jest-campaign-reporter.cjs` writes `<repo>/.campaign/runs/<artifact>.json` on every run, and `scripts/campaign-check.mjs:196` reads `<runsDir>/api.json`.

Verified: after `RUN_DB_SPECS=local DATABASE_URL=... npx jest --config jest.db.config.js`, `.campaign/runs/api.json` contained `numTotalTests 1` with the single suite `apps/api/src/common/testing/db-lane.db.spec.ts` — the full api lane's result had been replaced.

Failure scenario: a developer runs `npm run verify` (green), then `npm run local:test:db` to exercise the new lane, then re-runs `node scripts/campaign-check.mjs` on its own; the gate now reads a one-test artifact and reports proven ledger rows as unproven — a false RED. `npm run verify` itself is unaffected because it orders `turbo run test` before campaign-check, which is the caveat the reporter documents; the new lane simply adds a second writer to the same artifact name.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Override the reporter in jest.db.config.js — either `reporters: ["default"]`, or keep the campaign reporter under a distinct artifact name (`{ artifact: "api-db" }`) so the two lanes never write the same file.

confirmedFindings.summary: The R1 tripwire's raw-execution pattern is narrower than the invariant it claims to enforce: DDL issued via `$queryRawUnsafe` or through any client variable not literally named pool/client/db slips past it.
confirmedFindings.detail:
`EXEC_RAW_PATTERN = /(\$executeRaw(Unsafe)?\s*[(`]|\b(pool|client|db)\.query\s*[(`])/i` only recognises `$executeRaw`/`$executeRawUnsafe` and a `.query` call on the bare identifiers pool/client/db. The docstring states the broader invariant "Nothing under apps/api/src may issue runtime DDL".

Inputs that make the guard silently pass while runtime DDL exists:
- `await this.prisma.$queryRawUnsafe('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "X" (...)')` — Postgres executes DDL through a query just as happily as through execute, and `$queryRaw`/`$queryRawUnsafe` appear nowhere in the pattern.
- `await pgClient.query('ALTER TABLE ...')` or `await this.pgPool.query(...)` — `\b(pool|client|db)\.query` needs a word boundary immediately before the identifier, and in `pgClient` / `pgPool` the preceding character is a word character, so no boundary exists and the alternation does not match. (The `.` in `this.pgPool.query` likewise does not help: the boundary must precede `pool`, not `pgPool`.)

So the exact regression the tripwire exists to prevent — someone re-adding boot-time table creation — is caught only if they reuse the old spelling. The spec currently passes (verified: 4 suites, 14 tests green), so this is a coverage hole, not a present-day offender.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Widen EXEC_RAW_PATTERN to include `$queryRaw(Unsafe)?` and to match `.query(` on any receiver (e.g. `[\w$.]*(pool|client|db)\.query\s*[(`]/i` or simply `\.query\s*[(`]`), then re-run the tripwire across `apps/api/src` and, if the looser pattern produces false positives, narrow with an explicit allowlist rather than by name-shape.

confirmedFindings.summary: Architecture doc still states in the present tense that `main.ts:69` runs startup `ALTER TABLE` DDL gated by `RUN_STARTUP_DDL`, a function and flag this PR deletes; the file is owned by no package in the plan.
confirmedFindings.detail:
Line 221 reads: "**Startup DDL safety-net:** [`main.ts:69`](../apps/api/src/main.ts) runs idempotent `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` before boot, gated by `RUN_STARTUP_DDL` (defaults on) …". After the p1 deletion, `runStartupMigration` and the `RUN_STARTUP_DDL` gate no longer exist anywhere in `apps/api/src` (repo-wide grep for `RUN_STARTUP_DDL|runStartupMigration` returns only this line, two `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` proposal lines, the code-map, the pipeline artifacts, and the tripwire spec's explanatory comment), and `apps/api/src/main.ts` line 69 is now inside `bootstrap()`.

Failure scenario: an operator debugging a missing column reads this doc, believes a boot-time safety net will add it on the next deploy, and does not run the migration. p7 owned CLAUDE.md, the code map and docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md, but this file is in no package's file list, so nothing corrected it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Rewrite line 221 to record the safety net as removed by this PR and point at the replacement (`apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs` + the `Schema drift` step in `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml`), dropping the stale `main.ts:69` anchor.

confirmedFindings.summary: The production migration script now falls open onto an arbitrary DATABASE_URL instead of refusing when the Railway proxy vars are incomplete, and its only target-confirmation line then prints "undefined:undefined".
confirmedFindings.detail: Before this change prod-migrate.mjs computed `missing = need.filter(k => !e[k])` and, if ANY of the five proxy vars was absent, printed `Missing env: …` and `process.exit(1)` unconditionally — it could not run outside `railway run --service postgres`. After the swap to `resolveDatabaseUrl` (apps/api/scripts/lib/railway-db-url.mjs:16-28) the missing-var branch returns `env.DATABASE_URL` whenever that is set, so the script proceeds to `npx prisma migrate deploy` against whatever DATABASE_URL is in the environment. Concrete scenario: an operator or agent runs `node apps/api/scripts/prod-migrate.mjs` from a shell that exported DATABASE_URL for local work — the repo itself exports exactly `postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev` in root `local:seed`, `local:drift` and `local:test:db` — and forgets the `railway run --service postgres` prefix. The old script refused; the new one runs migrate deploy against the local database and reports success. Compounding it, line 36 still prints `Target host: ${e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN}:${e.RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT}`, which on this new fallback path renders `Target host: undefined:undefined` — so the operator's one confirmation of which database is about to be migrated is blank precisely on the path that was never supposed to exist. (The p3 engineer flagged both halves in the deviation note; neither was fixed.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Keep the fail-closed pre-check in prod-migrate.mjs: compute the missing proxy vars (export RAILWAY_PROXY_VARS from the helper) and exit 1 with the original guidance message before calling resolveDatabaseUrl, so the DATABASE_URL fallback is available to schema-drift.mjs but never to the prod deploy path. Then print the target with `redactUrl(url)` instead of the two raw proxy env vars.

confirmedFindings.summary: Any non-zero `prisma migrate status` aborts the drift check with exit 1 and the bare message "migrate status failed", so the tool answers nothing in the pending-migrations case it will most often be pointed at.
confirmedFindings.detail: `migrate status` exits non-zero for benign reasons — pending migrations, or a migration history that differs from the database's `_prisma_migrations` rows. prod-migrate.mjs:41-45 documents exactly this and deliberately swallows it ("`migrate status` exits non-zero when migrations are pending — that's expected"). schema-drift.mjs treats the same condition as fatal: it prints only `schema-drift: migrate status failed`, exits 1, and never runs the `migrate diff` that is the point of the script. Verified this session: `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev node scripts/schema-drift.mjs` against the running compose Postgres printed the pending/unknown-migration listing followed by `schema-drift: migrate status failed`, EXIT=1, with zero drift information. Two consequences. (1) CLAUDE.md as edited by this PR now tells operators "Any schema PR runs it against prod after deploy — `railway run --service postgres node apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs` — and requires exit 0"; run before the deploy, or on any environment with a pending migration, that returns 1 with a message that reads like a tool malfunction rather than "you have N pending migrations". (2) `local:validate` — the documented pre-PR gate — now ends in `&& npm run local:drift`, so the gate goes red for this reason alone on any dev database not brought up through the compose `migrate` one-shot. Note the happy path is fine: on a freshly replayed database the script exits 0 (verified).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Distinguish the cases: capture `migrate status` output and treat "pending migrations" as informational (report the count and continue to the diff), reserving exit 1 for a genuine failure (non-zero with no recognizable status output). At minimum, echo prisma's own status text into the failure line instead of the opaque "migrate status failed", and still run the diff so the operator gets the drift answer they invoked the script for.

confirmedFindings.summary: `describeDb` does not actually skip the suite — Jest executes a `describe.skip` callback during collection, so the DB lane throws instead of no-opping when RUN_DB_SPECS is unset.
confirmedFindings.detail: `describeDb` selects `describe.skip` when RUN_DB_SPECS is absent, but jest-circus still runs the describe callback to collect its children; only the tests are marked skipped. The shipped example puts `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()` in the describe body (db-lane.db.spec.ts:7), so it executes and throws. Verified this session: `npx jest --config jest.db.config.js` with RUN_DB_SPECS unset produced `Test Suites: 1 failed, 1 total / Tests: 0 total` with the stack `at requireLocalDatabaseUrl (common/testing/db-spec.ts:5:19) → at common/testing/db-lane.db.spec.ts:7:51 → at describeDb (common/testing/db-spec.ts:16:56)`. So `npm run test:db -w apps/api` — a script this PR adds and CLAUDE.md/code-map now advertise — hard-fails for any developer who runs it without the env prefix, and every future `*.db.spec.ts` that copies the shipped pattern inherits the failure. It also makes the code-map entry added by p7 wrong where it states `describeDb(name, fn)` is "gated on RUN_DB_SPECS being set, so the lane no-ops without it". Secondary effect: the `pg` Pool and PrismaClient in the body are constructed during collection even in the "skipped" run, while the `afterAll` that closes them never fires. (The happy path works: with RUN_DB_SPECS=local and a local DATABASE_URL the lane passes, verified.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Make describeDb genuinely inert — e.g. `if (!process.env.RUN_DB_SPECS) { describe.skip(name, () => { it.todo("requires RUN_DB_SPECS"); }); return; } describe(name, fn);` — or move `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()`/client construction into `beforeAll` in the spec template so nothing runs at collection time. Whichever is chosen, update the db-lane example and the code-map wording to match.

confirmedFindings.summary: `--dry-run` prints "NO DRIFT — database matches prisma/schema.prisma" and exits 0 without contacting any database.
confirmedFindings.detail: The `run()` stub returns `{ status: 0 }` for both the status and the diff invocation, so control falls into the `diff.status === 0` branch and the script emits the success sentence and exit 0. Verified this session: `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev node scripts/schema-drift.mjs --dry-run` printed the target line, two `[dry-run]` lines, then `schema-drift: NO DRIFT — database matches prisma/schema.prisma`, EXIT=0 — against a database that, when actually checked moments later, could not even complete `migrate status`. Anyone who lands `--dry-run` in a wrapper, a CI step, or a copied runbook line gets a green that asserts a fact never verified. The build plan explicitly specified the opposite: "Under `--dry-run` the target line and the two `[dry-run]` lines are the whole output".
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Return from the script after the dry-run listing (e.g. `if (dryRun) { console.log(...) ; process.exit(0); }` before invoking the status/diff sequence), or have the dry-run path print a distinct line such as `schema-drift: dry run — nothing checked` instead of the NO DRIFT sentence.

confirmedFindings.summary: The "Runtime-provisioned tables" comment block still tells the reader that PlatformConfig and AiUsageEvent are created at boot by the application, which this PR made false.
confirmedFindings.detail: schema.prisma:4050-4058 reads "Both tables are created at boot by the application itself, via raw `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (PlatformConfigService and RoutesService) … Declaring them here is what stops that". PlatformConfigService no longer issues that DDL (its onModuleInit was deleted), and 0_init already creates both tables plus `AiUsageEvent_createdAt_idx` (verified: migration.sql lines 940, 2166, 2631, 3345). This comment is the only in-schema explanation of why those two models exist and why their `dbgenerated` defaults are shaped the way they are; a future engineer trusting it could delete or reshape them believing the application will recreate them at boot, which would now be a silent data-loss path for the AI metering log. No implementation package owned schema.prisma, so nobody updated it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Rewrite the block header to say the tables are migration-owned as of PR-1 (`imp-03a`), keep the historical note about why the models were declared (so `migrate diff` would not emit DROP TABLE), and narrow the remaining runtime-writer mention to RoutesService's raw reads/writes of IdempotencyKey, which are DML, not DDL.

confirmedFindings.summary: The `"::1"` entry in LOCAL_HOSTS can never match, because `new URL(...).hostname` returns IPv6 hosts bracketed.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified this session: `new URL('postgresql://u:p@[::1]:5432/d').hostname` returns the string `"[::1]"`, not `"::1"`. So a developer whose DATABASE_URL uses the IPv6 loopback is refused with "Refusing to run DB-backed specs against non-local host [::1]" despite that being the most local host there is. The failure is fail-closed, so there is no safety hole — only a dead allowlist entry and a confusing refusal on IPv6-first setups.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add "[::1]" to LOCAL_HOSTS (keeping "::1" costs nothing), or strip surrounding brackets from `host` before the lookup.

confirmedFindings.summary: Adopting the shared helper silently removed prod-migrate's hard "Missing env" abort, so a partially-injected Railway env now runs `prisma migrate deploy` against whatever DATABASE_URL happens to be in scope.
confirmedFindings.detail: Before: `need.filter(...)` -> any of the 5 proxy vars missing => print `Missing env: <list>` and exit 1 unconditionally (old :29-36). After: `resolveDatabaseUrl(e)` (apps/api/scripts/lib/railway-db-url.mjs:24) falls back to `env.DATABASE_URL` whenever it is set, and only throws when DATABASE_URL is ALSO absent. Concrete failure: an operator runs `node apps/api/scripts/prod-migrate.mjs` from a shell where a local `.env` has exported DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev and RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_* are unset (i.e. they forgot the `railway run --service postgres` prefix). Old behaviour: exit 1 with the guidance line. New behaviour: line 36 prints `Target host: undefined:undefined`, then line 48 runs `prisma migrate deploy` against the developer's local database with no warning. Under `railway run --service postgres` with one proxy var missing it instead proceeds against the unreachable *.railway.internal host and fails at connect rather than with the clean message. R4 requires the `need`/error semantics be kept identical; they are not. (Reported by the p3 engineer as a deviation, not fixed.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint:
Re-add an explicit pre-check in prod-migrate.mjs before calling the helper: `const missing = RAILWAY_PROXY_VARS.filter((k) => !e[k]); if (missing.length) { console.error(`
Missing env: ${missing.join(", ")}
Run this via: railway run --service postgres node scripts/prod-migrate.mjs
`); process.exit(1); }` (import RAILWAY_PROXY_VARS from the helper), and change line 36 to print `redactUrl(url)` instead of the two raw env vars.

confirmedFindings.summary: `describeDb`'s skip is defeated — the describe body calls `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()` at collection time, so `npm run test:db -w apps/api` without env fails the suite instead of skipping it.
confirmedFindings.detail: Jest (circus) executes a `describe.skip` callback body; only the tests inside are skipped. db-lane.db.spec.ts calls `requireLocalDatabaseUrl()` and constructs the Pool/PrismaClient directly in the describe body (lines 7-9), so the throw happens during collection regardless of the skip. Verified by running `cd apps/api && DATABASE_URL= RUN_DB_SPECS= npx jest --config jest.db.config.js`: output is `FAIL src/common/testing/db-lane.db.spec.ts — Test suite failed to run: DB-backed specs need DATABASE_URL`, `Test Suites: 1 failed`, `Tests: 0 total`, exit non-zero. R6 gives `describeDb` the explicit contract of calling `describe.skip` when `RUN_DB_SPECS` is unset (T4 asserts exactly that), and the lane's only consumer nullifies it: anyone who runs the documented `npm run test:db -w apps/api` script directly (rather than root `local:test:db`) gets a red suite, and the same happens to any future `*.db.spec.ts` written to this pattern.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move the env read and client construction out of the describe body into lazily-run hooks, e.g. `describeDb("db lane", () => { let pool: Pool; let prisma: PrismaClient; beforeAll(() => { pool = new Pool({ connectionString: requireLocalDatabaseUrl() }); prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg(pool) }); }); afterAll(async () => { await prisma?.$disconnect(); await pool?.end(); }); it(...) })`. Add a regression assertion to db-spec.spec.ts or the lane that `npx jest --config jest.db.config.js` with no RUN_DB_SPECS exits 0 with 0 tests.

confirmedFindings.summary: The extended `paths` filter omits `apps/api/package.json`, the file that defines the `test:db` script and the `testPathIgnorePatterns` the new lane depends on.
confirmedFindings.detail: R7 lists six patterns and they are all present, but the lane's definition actually lives in two files: `apps/api/jest.db.config.js` (listed) and `apps/api/package.json` (not listed — it holds `"test:db": "jest --config jest.db.config.js"`, `"db:drift"`, and the `jest.testPathIgnorePatterns` entry `\.db\.spec\.ts$` that keeps db specs out of the default run). confirmedFindings.summary: Item #3 is marked `shipped (PR-1)` in the new Status column while its own body still prescribes setting the RUN_STARTUP_DDL flag that this PR deletes.
confirmedFindings.detail: The Summary row 3 now says `shipped (PR-1)` (line 31), but the section it summarises still reads at line 100: "1. Convert the boot-time `ALTER TABLE`s into real Prisma migrations and set `RUN_STARTUP_DDL=false`." and at line 101-103 proposes `prisma migrate diff --from-url $DATABASE_URL --to-schema-datamodel …` — neither the flag (deleted) nor those flag names (the shipped script uses `--from-config-datasource --to-schema`) exist any more. Same file, same commit, contradictory content.

confirmedFindings.detail: Row 7 now asserts `| 7 | P1 | **Local full-stack hosting via Docker (pre-PR)** | M | 🟡 | open |`. remainingFindings.summary: The job that hosts the new production-facing drift gate sets `NODE_ENV: test` at job level, which is exactly the condition `schema-drift.mjs` uses to arm its test-only `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI` stub — so the safety property the code, the test plan and CLAUDE.md all assert does not hold at the one place the gate actually runs.
remainingFindings.detail:
Evidence, read this session:

1. `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:69-71` — the `replay` job carries a job-level `env:` block containing `DATABASE_URL: …` and `NODE_ENV: test`. Job-level env applies to every step; the new `Schema drift (history → datamodel)` step (lines 88-92) overrides only `DATABASE_URL`, so it runs with `NODE_ENV=test`.

2. `apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs` (digest, new file): `const underTest = process.env.NODE_ENV === "test" || Boolean(process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID);` … `const prismaCli = override && underTest ? override : require.resolve("prisma/build/index.js", …)`. In the CI job `underTest` is TRUE. The only thing preventing the gate from spawning a stub is that `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI` happens to be unset.

3. `CLAUDE.md` (this diff, Deployment & DB safety) now states the opposite as a durable rule: the hook "is honoured only when `NODE_ENV=test` or `JEST_WORKER_ID` is set … and is ignored — loudly — anywhere else, so a stray export can never make the gate report NO DRIFT from a stub." For the CI gate, "anywhere else" is not where it runs.

4. The test that certifies the property, T3(h) in `apps/api/src/common/schema-drift-script.spec.ts`, explicitly does `delete env.NODE_ENV; delete env.JEST_WORKER_ID;` before spawning. It proves the guard holds in an environment the real gate never has. The test-plan mutation row ("a stray `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI` export makes the prod gate spawn a stub") is therefore satisfied literally and unmet in spirit for the CI gate.

Failure scenario: any later edit that adds `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI` to this workflow's env (a repo/org Actions variable wired in, a copy-paste of the stub setup from the spec file, a composite action that exports it) makes the `Schema drift (history → datamodel)` step spawn the stub, print `schema-drift: NO DRIFT — database matches prisma/schema.prisma`, exit 0, and the job stays green — with only a WARNING line in a log nobody reads on a green run. The gate that replaces the deleted boot-time DDL then certifies a database it never contacted. The same composition reaches prod: `apps/api/scripts/prod-migrate.mjs:63-67` spawns the drift check with `env` = the operator's full environment, so a shell that still has `NODE_ENV=test` set from a prior test run also arms the hook on the production post-deploy gate.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Do not key the hook off `NODE_ENV`/`JEST_WORKER_ID`, which the repo sets in CI and in dev shells. Gate the override on something only a test process can set and no gate ever has (e.g. require `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI_I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_IS_NOT_A_REAL_CHECK=1` alongside it), or drop `NODE_ENV: test` from the db-migrations job env and set it per-step only where needed. Then update the CLAUDE.md claim to match whatever the guard actually is, and make T3(h) assert the property under `NODE_ENV=test`, since that is the gate's real environment.
remainingFindings.decision: Job-level `NODE_ENV: test` in db-migrations.yml makes `underTest` true for the production-facing drift step, so the test-only `SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI` stub hook is armed at the one place the gate runs; only the accidental absence of that env var keeps the gate honest, and CLAUDE.md now asserts the opposite as a durable rule. Fix is small (gate the override on JEST_WORKER_ID alone, or unset NODE_ENV on that step) but the stated invariant is false as shipped.

remainingFindings.summary: The new DB-backed spec lane reports green when it executes zero tests, so the CI step that is supposed to prove the lane works cannot distinguish "ran and passed" from "skipped everything" — the exact failure mode L-041 was written for.
remainingFindings.detail:
Directly observed this session. Ran `npx jest --config jest.db.config.js` from `apps/api` with `RUN_DB_SPECS` unset:

```
Test Suites: 1 skipped, 0 of 1 total
Tests:       1 skipped, 1 total
Ran all test suites.
EXIT=0
```

So `npm run test:db -w apps/api` exits 0 having run nothing. `db-spec.ts:19-22` is why: `if (!process.env.RUN_DB_SPECS) { describe.skip(name, () => { it("skipped: RUN_DB_SPECS unset", () => {}); }); return; }` — the inert placeholder makes Jest report one skipped test and exit 0. Nothing in `apps/api/jest.db.config.js` or in the workflow asserts that any test actually executed (no `--onlyFailures`-style floor, no `passWithNoTests: false` equivalent for the all-skipped case, no post-step assertion on the run summary).

Failure scenario: `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:94-98` supplies `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci` for the `DB-backed specs` step. Drop, rename, or typo that env key in any future edit — or add a second caller of `test:db` that forgets it — and the step passes green while executing zero database assertions. The acceptance oracle A3 ("lane: `db-lane.db.spec.ts` 1 passed") is a human close-out step, not an automated one, so nothing on the PR path would catch it. This is the shape of `.claude/lessons/LESSONS.md` L-041 (lines 14-27): "a green job that ran zero tests … a suite is green when a test is skipped; neither says your proof ran." The lane exists precisely so future PRs (order-merge advisory lock, cron leader lock, findUnique tenancy pins — discovery.md) can prove database behaviour; a lane that is green when silent will certify those too.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Make the lane fail closed when it is asked to run but cannot: have the CI step assert execution (e.g. `jest --config jest.db.config.js --ci` plus a check that the summary shows a passed test, or run the lane with an explicit `RUN_DB_SPECS` requirement that throws in `globalSetup` rather than skipping when the config is the db config). At minimum, make `jest.db.config.js` treat an all-skipped run as a failure, since the default `test:db` invocation and the CI invocation are the same command.
remainingFindings.decision: Observed `1 skipped, EXIT=0` with RUN_DB_SPECS unset: the lane reports green having executed nothing, so a dropped or mistyped `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci` in the workflow turns the proving step into a silent no-op — the steps>0 rule this repo already pays for. It needs a future edit to bite, so minor, but a CI-mode floor (fail when CI is set and the lane skipped) is cheap.

remainingFindings.summary: `RUN_DB_SPECS=ci` is a single env value that both enables the DB lane and disables its refusal to connect to a non-local host, and the lane is a new database-touching test entry point that never calls the repo's mandatory `assertTestTenant` guard.
remainingFindings.detail:
Two guards are collapsed into one switch:

- `db-spec.ts:19` — `describeDb` runs the suite for ANY truthy `RUN_DB_SPECS`.
- `db-spec.ts:8-11` — `requireLocalDatabaseUrl` refuses a non-local host `if (!LOCAL_HOSTS.has(host) && env.RUN_DB_SPECS !== "ci")`, with the message "(set RUN_DB_SPECS=ci only in CI)".

So the one value a developer is most likely to copy is the value that turns the host guard off. And the value is published in a checked-in file they are told to mirror: `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:94-98` sets `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci`.

Meanwhile `CLAUDE.md` ("Test tenants & real-client data (POLICY — no exceptions)") states: "Enforced in code by `scripts/lib/test-tenants.cjs` (`assertTestTenant`); every tenant-scoped script/test entry point must call it before any write." I confirmed `scripts/lib/test-tenants.cjs:32` exports `assertTestTenant`. Neither `db-spec.ts`, `jest.db.config.js`, nor `db-lane.db.spec.ts` calls it, and nothing in the lane's design requires a future `*.db.spec.ts` to.

Failure scenario: a developer reproducing a CI failure runs `RUN_DB_SPECS=ci npm run test:db -w apps/api` (the exact incantation the workflow models) in a shell where `DATABASE_URL` is already exported — from `npm run local:drift`, from `apps/api/.env`, or from a `railway run --service postgres` session, which is the URL shape `prod-migrate.mjs`/`scripts/lib/railway-db-url.mjs` teach them to build. The host guard is disabled by the same variable that enabled the lane, no tenant guard runs, and the lane connects to production. Today the only member is a harmless `SELECT 1` (`db-lane.db.spec.ts`), but discovery.md states the lane exists for advisory-lock, cron-leader-lock and tenancy-pin specs — i.e. specs that will write. `jest.db.config.js` also raises `testTimeout` to 30000, so a slow production connection succeeds rather than timing out.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Split the two concerns: one variable to opt into the lane, a separate explicit one (or a CI-only signal such as `GITHUB_ACTIONS`) to permit a non-local host, so the enabling value is never also the bypass. And enroll the lane in the existing policy — have `requireLocalDatabaseUrl` (or a lane-level setup file) call `assertTestTenant` for any tenant slug a db spec targets, per CLAUDE.md's "every tenant-scoped script/test entry point".
remainingFindings.decision: The single value `RUN_DB_SPECS=ci` both enables the lane and disables the non-local-host refusal, and it is the value published in the checked-in workflow that developers copy — so the only guard between this new DB-touching entry point and a real database is defeated by its most likely invocation. The repo's test-tenant policy is explicit and no-exceptions; the lane should not carry a bypass at all if CI's Postgres is reachable on a local host (see gap).

remainingFindings.detail:
The T1 tripwire (`apps/api/src/common/no-runtime-ddl.spec.ts:12`, `SRC_ROOT = join(__dirname, "..")`) walks only `apps/api/src`. I ran its exact predicate over that tree this session: `OFFENDERS: []` — green. I then ran the DDL half over all of `apps/api` excluding `migrations/` and found three unenrolled writers under `apps/api/scripts/`:

- `add-invoice-defaults-columns.js:6-8` — `await c.query('ALTER TABLE "TenantConfig" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "invoiceNotes" TEXT, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "invoiceTerms" TEXT')`. This is byte-for-byte the first statement this PR just deleted from `runStartupMigration()` in `main.ts`. Line 2: `const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL || "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev"` — it does not fail closed on a missing URL.
- `run-variant-name-migration.js` — its own header documents the invocation `railway run node apps/api/scripts/run-variant-name-migration.js`, i.e. this class of script is explicitly run against production by hand; it drops and creates unique indexes.

remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide the disposition of `apps/api/scripts/{add-invoice-defaults-columns,run-variant-name-migration,apply-rls}.js` in this PR rather than leaving them: delete the two whose DDL is already in the migration history (`add-invoice-defaults-columns.js`'s columns are in `0_init/migration.sql:243-244`, confirmed), or, if `apply-rls.js` must stay for the parked RLS work, widen the tripwire's root to `apps/api` with an explicit, named allowlist so the exception is visible, and say in CLAUDE.md which schema writers survive.
remainingFindings.decision: A runnable script byte-identical to the DDL this PR retired, plus two sibling schema writers, remain under apps/api/scripts outside the tripwire's src-only scan, and one defaults to a hardcoded URL instead of failing closed. They are manual, not boot-time, so they are a scope gap of the 'schema changes only via migrations' program rather than a defect in the shipped behaviour — delete them or enroll scripts/ in the tripwire in PR-2.

remainingFindings.summary: L-052's durable Lesson line prescribes grepping `$executeRaw*` DDL sites — the exact too-narrow grep this run proved insufficient, since the `main.ts` DDL it retired went through a raw `pg` `Pool.query`, not `$executeRaw*`.
remainingFindings.detail:
`.claude/lessons/LESSONS.md:113` (added by this PR): "**Lesson:** retiring a runtime schema writer means grepping every `$executeRaw*` DDL site, proving the live DB already matches the datamodel … before deleting…"

That instruction would have missed the primary site this PR removed. Evidence from the diff itself: `main.ts`'s deleted `runStartupMigration()` issued its `ALTER TABLE` statements as `await pool.query(...)` on a `new Pool(...)` from `pg` — there is no `$executeRaw` anywhere in the deleted block. The run's own artifacts say so explicitly and correct for it everywhere EXCEPT the register:
- test-plan T1: "The third shape — `<any receiver>.query(` — is load-bearing, not decoration: `main.ts` issued its DDL through `new Pool(...).query(...)`, never `$executeRaw*`, so a `$executeRaw`-only predicate would not list it."
- `no-runtime-ddl.spec.ts:29` implements all three shapes.
- `CLAUDE.md` (this diff) gets it right: "a grep for runtime DDL must cover `$executeRaw`, `$executeRawUnsafe`/`$queryRaw*`, and `.query(` on a pg client."

Only the lessons register — the artifact the project reads before every major task and the one that outlives the PR — carries the narrow version. A file-scoped review of `LESSONS.md` finds it faithful to the spec's L-052 draft (spec.md line 51 has the same wording), so only a whole-diff read catches the contradiction.

Failure scenario: the next agent retiring a runtime schema writer follows L-052 literally, greps `$executeRaw*`, deletes those sites, declares the writer retired, and leaves a `pool.query("ALTER TABLE …")` site running on every boot — reproducing this exact bug with the lesson supposedly guarding against it.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Reword the Lesson line to the shape CLAUDE.md already uses: grep every raw-execution shape — `$executeRaw`, `$executeRawUnsafe`, `$queryRaw*`, and `<client>.query(` on a raw `pg` pool/client — not just `$executeRaw*`. Byte-neutral enough not to disturb the register's size budget (validator: 31.1/40.0 KB, exits 0).
remainingFindings.decision: L-052's Lesson line prescribes the `$executeRaw*` grep that the run itself proved insufficient — main.ts's DDL went through a pg `Pool.query` — while the test plan, the tripwire and CLAUDE.md all name the third shape. The register is the durable rule, so its text should match the three-shape predicate.

remainingFindings.summary: The tripwire's DDL half matches ordinary English prose, and one source file already satisfies it on a comment — so the gate is one routine edit away from a false red that can only be fixed by rewording a sentence.
remainingFindings.detail:
`no-runtime-ddl.spec.ts:30`: `const DDL_PATTERN = /\b(CREATE|ALTER|DROP)\s+(TABLE|INDEX|COLUMN|TYPE|SCHEMA)\b/i;` — case-insensitive, applied to the whole file text, with no attempt to require SQL context (no quote, no backtick, no adjacency to the raw-execution call).

I ran the tripwire's exact two predicates over `apps/api/src` this session. Result: `OFFENDERS: []` (green), but the breakdown is thin — **13 files match the raw-execution half, and exactly 1 file matches the DDL half**, and that one match is prose, not SQL:

`apps/api/src/authorizations/authorization-overrides.service.ts:33` — `// forTenant() injects tenantId at runtime; the create type still requires it, so cast.` The words "create type" satisfy `CREATE\s+TYPE` under `/i`. That file contains no raw execution at all today (grep for `$executeRaw*|.query(` returns nothing), which is the only reason the suite is green.

Failure scenario: `authorization-overrides.service.ts` gains any raw read — `this.prisma.$queryRaw`…`` for a permissions lookup, or a `queryBus.query(` / repository `.query(` call, both of which the deliberately-broad `\b[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\.query\s*[(\`]` half matches — and `npm run verify` goes red with `Expected: [] / Received: ["authorizations/authorization-overrides.service.ts"]`, a message that accuses the file of issuing runtime DDL when the only trigger is an English sentence. The prescribed remedy is then to reword a comment, which is exactly the kind of unexplainable gate the next person disables. Symmetrically, the same looseness in the other direction is untested: nothing pins the DDL half against a legitimate SQL string, so a future tightening could silently un-catch real DDL.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Require some SQL context before treating a DDL keyword as a finding — match only inside a string/template literal, or require the DDL keyword to be followed by a quoted identifier (`"Table"`) as every real site in this repo is. Add a negative case to the `it.each` table (an English comment containing "create type") so the narrowing is pinned by a test rather than left to the next reader.
remainingFindings.decision: The case-insensitive DDL pattern matches English prose and already hits a comment (`create type`) in a file kept green only because it has no raw-execution call; a routine comment in any of the 13 raw-execution files would false-red the tripwire. Anchor the DDL match to SQL context (inside a string/template or adjacent to the call) rather than bare words.

remainingFindings.summary: `local:drift` sets a compose DATABASE_URL that `resolveDatabaseUrl` then discards — Railway proxy vars in the developer's shell win, so the local pre-PR gate reports its verdict against production instead of the compose Postgres.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by reading.

The chain: `package.json:32` `local:validate` now ends `&& npm run local:drift`. `package.json:30` `local:drift` = `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-user}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-pass}@localhost:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-routeflow_dev}" sh -c 'npm run db:drift -w apps/api'`. `apps/api/package.json` `db:drift` = `node scripts/schema-drift.mjs`. `schema-drift.mjs:` calls `resolveDatabaseUrl(process.env)` from `apps/api/scripts/lib/railway-db-url.mjs`, whose contract (lines 18-30) is: if all five of POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB, RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN, RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT are set, build the proxy URL and RETURN IT; only `if (missing.length !== 0)` does it fall through to `env.DATABASE_URL`. The env-var prefix `local:drift` sets is therefore inert whenever those five vars are inherited from the parent shell — nothing in `local:drift`, `schema-drift.mjs`, or the helper unsets or overrides them, and the script has no `--local` / `--url-from-env` flag and no host allowlist (contrast `db-spec.ts:1-11`, which DOES enforce one for the sibling `local:test:db` lane).

I ran the exact URL string `local:drift` produces against the exact five-var state a Railway shell supplies:

  env -u ... DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/routeflow_dev" \
    POSTGRES_USER=railwayuser POSTGRES_PASSWORD=railwaypw POSTGRES_DB=railway \
    RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN=fake-proxy.rlwy.net RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT=41234 \
    node apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs --dry-run

  schema-drift: target postgresql://railwayuser:***@fake-proxy.rlwy.net:41234/railway

The localhost URL was discarded. That five-var state is not hypothetical here: it is the design premise the script's own header comment (schema-drift.mjs:6-9) cites — "under `railway run --service postgres` DATABASE_URL is the unreachable *.railway.internal host" — i.e. under Railway all five proxy vars co-exist, which is exactly the environment CLAUDE.md tells the operator to work in for prod DB access (`railway run --service postgres node <script>`).

FAILURE SCENARIO (false all-clear, the gate's whole purpose): developer adds a migration, runs `npm run local:up` but forgets `npm run local:migrate`, so the compose DB is genuinely drifted. Their shell still carries the Railway vars from earlier prod work. `npm run local:validate` runs smoke + post-deploy-check against localhost:3000 (correct), then `local:drift` resolves to PRODUCTION, where the datamodel does match, prints `schema-drift: NO DRIFT — database matches prisma/schema.prisma`, exits 0. `local:validate` goes green. The developer ships believing the local stack was drift-checked; it never was, and the one line naming the real target is buried mid-log.

SECOND SCENARIO (hybrid URL, same root cause): `docker-compose.yml:119` and all three of `local:seed`/`local:drift`/`local:test:db` use `${POSTGRES_USER:-user}` / `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-pass}` / `${POSTGRES_DB:-routeflow_dev}`, so the repo actively invites a developer to export those three to customise local compose credentials. With those three set locally plus RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN/PORT in scope, `resolveDatabaseUrl` sees five present and builds LOCAL credentials against the PRODUCTION proxy host:port — a URL that is neither. It fails auth and the gate exits 1 with "database unreachable or CLI error", failing `local:validate` for a reason the message never names.

POLICY CONTRADICTION: CLAUDE.md's Guardrails state `local:validate` "runs **only** against the approved **test** tenant … never a live tenant (enforced by `assertTestTenant`)". The step this PR appends to `local:validate` has no such enforcement and can open a connection from a developer laptop to the production database. The connection is read-only (`migrate status` + `migrate diff --from-config-datasource`, and `prisma.config.ts` reads `process.env.DATABASE_URL` directly with no dotenv override, so the resolved URL is honoured verbatim) — so no data is at risk — but the verdict is about the wrong database and the guardrail sentence is now false.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Make the local gate pin the local URL rather than inheriting the prod-oriented precedence. Cheapest: have `local:drift`/`local:test:db` clear the proxy vars for the child, e.g. `sh -c 'unset POSTGRES_USER POSTGRES_PASSWORD POSTGRES_DB RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN RAILWAY_TCP_PROXY_PORT; npm run db:drift -w apps/api'`. Cleaner: add a `--url-from-env` (or `--local`) flag to schema-drift.mjs that bypasses `resolveDatabaseUrl`'s proxy branch and uses DATABASE_URL verbatim, and use it in `local:drift`; keep the proxy-wins precedence for the prod path (spec R3) untouched. Either way, also reconcile the CLAUDE.md guardrail sentence about `local:validate` never touching a live target.
remainingFindings.decision: Verified by execution: resolveDatabaseUrl returns the Railway proxy URL whenever all five proxy vars are present and only falls through to DATABASE_URL when one is missing, so the env prefix `local:drift` sets is inert in any shell that inherited Railway env (e.g. after `railway run`/`railway shell`). The gate is read-only so no data is at risk, but `local:validate` would then print a prod verdict labelled as the local pre-PR check with no indication of the target — the fix is either an explicit-URL mode for schema-drift.mjs (`--url-from-env` / DATABASE_URL-wins-when-explicitly-passed) or having `local:drift` unset the five proxy vars, plus a printed scrubbed target host so the operator can see which DB was checked.

remainingFindings.summary: The `underTest` predicate accepts `NODE_ENV=test`, and `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:71` sets `NODE_ENV: test` job-wide — so the SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI stub-guard is disarmed in the only automated consumer of the drift gate.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY EXECUTION.

`schema-drift.mjs:46-49`:
  const underTest = process.env.NODE_ENV === "test" || Boolean(process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID);
  const override = process.env.SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI;
  const prismaCli = override && underTest ? override : require.resolve("prisma/build/index.js", …);

The stated purpose of the `underTest` conjunct (schema-drift.mjs:43-45 comment, and test-plan.md mutation-probe row T3(h)) is: "a stray SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI export makes the prod gate spawn a stub" — the guard exists so the gate cannot be turned into a stub that reports NO DRIFT.

`.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:69-71` sets job-level env:
  env:
    DATABASE_URL: postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/routeflow_test
    NODE_ENV: test

The "Schema drift (history → datamodel)" step (lines 88-92) supplies a step-level `env:` that overrides only DATABASE_URL, so `NODE_ENV: test` is in effect for it. There is no JEST process involved — the step is a bare `node scripts/schema-drift.mjs` — yet `underTest` evaluates true.

I reproduced the CI environment exactly (NODE_ENV=test, JEST_WORKER_ID explicitly unset, a 3-line stub script as the CLI):

  env -u JEST_WORKER_ID … NODE_ENV=test \
    DATABASE_URL="postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/routeflow_test" \
    SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI="$TEMP/stub-prisma.mjs" node apps/api/scripts/schema-drift.mjs

  schema-drift: WARNING — SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI override in effect; this is NOT a real drift check
  schema-drift: target postgresql://test:***@localhost:5432/routeflow_test
  STUB PRISMA RAN: migrate status
  STUB PRISMA RAN: migrate diff --from-config-datasource --to-schema prisma/schema.prisma --script --exit-code
  schema-drift: NO DRIFT — database matches prisma/schema.prisma
  EXIT=0

The gate printed its verdict and exited 0 without contacting any database.

FAILURE SCENARIO: any repo-level or org-level Actions variable named SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI, any composite/reusable action or future step that exports it into the `replay` job, or anyone copying the workflow's `NODE_ENV: test` idiom into a job that also carries that variable, silently converts the schema-drift gate into a stub that always reports NO DRIFT and exits 0. The only signal is one WARNING line on stderr of a step nobody reads on a green run. The class of failure this whole PR exists to prevent — a schema gate that is green without checking — is reachable through the guard that was written to prevent it.

WHY NO TEST CATCHES IT: `apps/api/src/common/schema-drift-script.spec.ts` T3(h) (lines 183-192) proves the ignore path only by deleting BOTH `NODE_ENV` and `JEST_WORKER_ID` from the child env, and its own comment at line 122 says "NODE_ENV is passed explicitly (never relying on an inherited JEST_WORKER_ID)". No test asserts the guard closes under `NODE_ENV=test` alone, which is precisely the CI job's environment.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Narrow the predicate to the signal that actually means "inside a jest process": `const underTest = Boolean(process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID);` (the spec's own spawn tests inherit JEST_WORKER_ID, and T3's other cases can pass it explicitly instead of NODE_ENV). Alternatively keep NODE_ENV but require JEST_WORKER_ID as well. Either way add a T3 case asserting the override is IGNORED with `NODE_ENV=test` and no JEST_WORKER_ID, so the CI environment is covered.
remainingFindings.decision: Verified: `NODE_ENV: test` is job-wide in db-migrations.yml and the drift step's env override only replaces DATABASE_URL, so the `underTest` conjunct that is supposed to keep SCHEMA_DRIFT_PRISMA_CLI from stubbing the gate is satisfied in CI. Blast radius is small — the workflow env is the only source of variables on a runner, so a stub would need a reviewed edit to the workflow, and the CI gate checks a fresh throwaway Postgres rather than prod — but the guard is disarmed in the only automated consumer and contradicts the invariant the T3(h) mutation probe claims to enforce. Fix: gate the override on JEST_WORKER_ID alone (or set NODE_ENV explicitly in the drift step).

remainingFindings.summary: The `RUN_DB_SPECS === "ci"` host-guard bypass has no consumer — the CI step's DATABASE_URL host is `localhost`, already in LOCAL_HOSTS — so it is a dead escape hatch that only weakens the guard and teaches how to point the DB lane at production.
remainingFindings.detail:
ANSWERING THE FOCUSED QUESTION DIRECTLY: the `DB-backed specs` step's DATABASE_URL resolves to a LOCAL host.

`.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:94-98`:
  - name: DB-backed specs
    run: npm run test:db -w apps/api
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://test:test@localhost:5432/routeflow_test
      RUN_DB_SPECS: ci

The job uses a GitHub Actions service container (lines 54-67) with `ports: - 5432:5432`, so the database is reachable on the runner as `localhost:5432` — the URL is a literal `localhost`, not a `postgres` service hostname and not a remote host.

`apps/api/src/common/testing/db-spec.ts:1-11`:
  const LOCAL_HOSTS = new Set(["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "postgres", "db"]);
  …
  if (!LOCAL_HOSTS.has(host) && env.RUN_DB_SPECS !== "ci") { throw … }

`localhost` is in LOCAL_HOSTS, so `!LOCAL_HOSTS.has(host)` is false and the `RUN_DB_SPECS !== "ci"` conjunct is never reached by the CI caller. A repo-wide grep for RUN_DB_SPECS (excluding node_modules) returns exactly two producers: `.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml:98` (`ci`, host localhost) and `package.json:31` `local:test:db` (`local`, host localhost). No caller anywhere sets RUN_DB_SPECS=ci with a non-local host. The only thing exercising the bypass branch is `db-spec.spec.ts:52-54` (T4(c)), a test written to enshrine it.

Note RUN_DB_SPECS itself is NOT dead — `describeDb` (db-spec.ts:19) needs any truthy value to un-skip the lane — so deleting the `&& env.RUN_DB_SPECS !== "ci"` conjunct costs CI nothing: the step keeps passing on the `localhost` host check, and `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci` keeps un-skipping the suite.

FAILURE SCENARIO (why the dead branch is not merely tidy-up): the DB lane exists to grow — R6 establishes it precisely so future specs can touch a real database, and those will create/truncate rows rather than `SELECT 1`. The only thing standing between `npm run test:db -w apps/api` and a production database is the LOCAL_HOSTS check, and `RUN_DB_SPECS=ci` disables it for ANY host with no second factor. The thrown message (db-spec.ts:10) even documents the escape: "set RUN_DB_SPECS=ci only in CI". A developer following this repo's own documented prod-access idiom — CLAUDE.md: "Prod DB access goes through `railway run --service postgres node <script>`" — running `railway run --service postgres npm run test:db -w apps/api` with RUN_DB_SPECS=ci copied from the workflow gets a DB lane connected straight to production, past the only guard, with no tenant assertion (`assertTestTenant` is not in this path). Deleting the conjunct removes that path entirely and breaks nothing that exists today.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Delete the `&& env.RUN_DB_SPECS !== "ci"` conjunct from db-spec.ts:8 so the host allowlist is unconditional, and drop T4(c) (`db-spec.spec.ts:52-54`) which exists only to assert the removed branch. CI is unaffected: the workflow's host is `localhost`, and `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci` remains load-bearing for `describeDb`. Update the spec R6 sentence and `.claude/code-map/api.md:67` which both still describe the bypass. If a future non-local CI host is genuinely needed, reintroduce it as an explicit allowlist entry rather than a blanket bypass.
remainingFindings.decision: Directly answers the focused question: the DB-backed specs step's DATABASE_URL is a literal `localhost:5432` against a service container, which is already in LOCAL_HOSTS, so the `RUN_DB_SPECS === "ci"` short-circuit is never reached and has no consumer. It is dead code whose only effect is to document a one-word way to point the DB lane at a non-local host. Delete the bypass outright; the step's `RUN_DB_SPECS: ci` remains a truthy enable value for describeDb, so nothing else changes.
